content.comment_body: I have encountered several problems. I am using [product_name] [product_name] [version_no] (fully licensed, English language), and there are no updates available—it's still [version_no]. When I try to export the program to a BIN file, I get a 'java.lang.NullPointerException' error. If I attempt to open a .bin file generated by the software, it prompts with 'You must use newer version of this program.' Exporting the program to an SD card fails with 'no card found,' even though the card is inserted and the LOGO_U_P.bin file can be opened. Is there really no update for [version_no]? If not, does anyone know how to resolve these issues?

As far as I know, there isn't an update for [product_name] [version_no]. I'm also using [product_name] [version_no]. To address issues, I create a .bin file and copy it to the SD card. If needed, you can upload your file here, and I can generate a .bin file for you.

Thanks for offering help, but I need to create multiple .bin files, so that solution doesn't work for me. The main issue is that exporting to SD card fails. Creating BIN files is only a partial workaround. I suspect IO-related functions of [product_name] are more reliable on Windows, so I plan to try switching from Linux to Windows to resolve the SD card export problem.

Check the folder path where your [product_name] program is stored on your computer. From experience, if the path name contains non-English characters or is too long, [product_name] may encounter issues. Try saving the file in a shorter path, like the root directory of C or D drive in Windows.
Thanks for the suggestion, but my path only includes English characters.

A potential workaround is to dedicate one temporary [product_name] (with display) for conversion. Format the SD card on your computer (FAT32, default settings), transfer the target program (including IP address) to the temporary device, and save the program to the SD card. Finally, insert the SD card into the target device and power it on. This requires more steps and network configuration, but it works. Remember, both the program and SD card store IP settings and load them during power-up.
Which operating system are you using on your computer?
I'm running Linux, which meets the requirements for [product_name] [version_no].

I have additional details. There are two ways to export: 1) Using 'Save As' for diagrams; 2) Using 'Export' for network project's devices. The first method works fine, but exporting a network device results in the java.lang.NullPointerException error.

Try exporting the [product_name] diagram from your network project to a folder, then open the folder and start the exported file. You should be able to use 'Save As' to save the program as a .BIN file.

But does this method provide the same result as the 'save to SD card' function on [product_name] BM? Or could it miss certain parameters? I think this is why the network project offers an 'export' function.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encounter serious export issues using [product_name] [version_no], such as errors when attempting to export to BIN files or directly to SD cards. Efforts to export often result in Java errors or messages about needing newer program versions. Workarounds are complicated and suggest that IO-related functionality may work better on Windows, while Linux users face significant difficulties.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable export options for BIN files and SD cards, compatibility between software and hardware, and error-free operation regardless of their computer's operating system.
